database.note: This is a local dev database, not production. Production (Railway) uses the same schema via sqlite+aiosqlite at a different path/volume per app/core/config.py; absolute counts here reflect local dev state only, not production scale.

price_bars.note: daily, 49 real symbols + NIFTY50 index + NIFTYBEES ETF; ~5 years, real depth.

prediction_records_legacy.note: older PredictionRecord table, predates PriceBar/quant_research; overlapping purpose.

opportunities_v2.note: single shadow-run day, per this session's Opportunity Engine V2 work.

news_articles.note: see data_quality_findings — published_at is NOT a reliable timestamp for this table.

events.note: event_date column is 100% NULL across all rows — see data_quality_findings.

company_intelligence_observations.note: 2-day depth only — daily 5PM IST job appears to have produced no new rows since 2026-08-17, a 5+ day gap as of today 2026-08-23.

market_snapshots.note: only ONE row exists total — this table is designed append-only-per-day but has accumulated essentially nothing.

sector_data.note: upsert-in-place 'current state' table, stale since 2026-06-28 (~2 months as of today) — not a time series at all.

news_articles_published_at_is_unreliable.evidence: Sample raw values: '2h ago', '4h ago', '1d ago', '41m ago', a mojibake character, and some real ISO-ish date strings mixed in the SAME column. At least 332 of 6529 rows (~5%, rough LIKE-based count, likely an undercount) are unparseable relative-time strings, not real timestamps.
news_articles_published_at_is_unreliable.implication: This column can never be trusted for point-in-time ordering or historical analysis. created_at (real ingestion timestamp) is the only reliable temporal anchor on this table today, and it answers a different question (when MarketRipple ingested it, not when the source published it).

events_event_date_is_entirely_null.evidence: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE event_date IS NOT NULL -> 0, across all 3035 rows.
events_event_date_is_entirely_null.implication: published_at holds the real usable timestamp for this table instead; event_date appears to be a dead/never-populated column.

market_snapshots_effectively_empty.evidence: Exactly 1 row total, despite snapshot_type='close' being documented elsewhere in the codebase as DB-enforced immutable-once-per-day.
market_snapshots_effectively_empty.implication: Bank Nifty, India VIX, FII/DII, sector ranks — everything this table is meant to warehouse — has essentially zero real historical depth today, 1 data point.

sector_data_stale_not_a_time_series.evidence: 12 rows (one per sector), all updated_at = 2026-06-28, no historical rows of any kind.
sector_data_stale_not_a_time_series.implication: This is an upsert-in-place 'current state' table masquerading as something that could be read historically — using it as a historical feature would silently leak or mislead (same finding as Phase B0's quant leakage audit).

company_intelligence_observations_gap.evidence: Rows only exist for 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-17 despite a documented 5PM IST daily job; no rows for the 5+ days since, as of today 2026-08-23.
company_intelligence_observations_gap.implication: Unknown from local inspection alone whether this is a local-dev-server-not-running artifact or a real production stall — flagged, not diagnosed, in this audit.

known_limitations_of_this_snapshot: Local dev database only — production row counts/scale will differ.
Per-table byte size not measurable (no dbstat support in this SQLite build) — only total file size is real.
This snapshot does not attempt to classify every table's source/consumer/point-in-time-safety — that is Step 1/Step 2 of the Phase 1A audit, delivered separately.
No fabricated numbers anywhere in this file — every count and date range above was queried live against the real database at capture time.
